title: Richard Feynman never named that method, and there is no evidence he used it as a formal system.
description:
Richard Feynman never named that method, and there is no evidence he used it as a formal system. The four step version taught online today (pick a concept, explain it simply, spot where you get stuck, return to the source) was written up by somebody else, decades after he died.

A Canadian writer running a free self study course. On 1 September 2011 he posted a video called 'The Feynman Technique' as the opening lesson of a learning bootcamp, and the name spread from there.

In 2024 he wrote that the technique is 'only loosely based on Richard Feynman's practices'. Feynman died in 1988, twenty three years before that video existed. He was never consulted about a method carrying his name.

Preparing for his Princeton oral exams, he opened a notebook and wrote on the title page: NOTEBOOK OF THINGS I DON'T KNOW ABOUT. Biographer James Gleick describes him spending weeks taking every branch of physics apart, hunting for the gaps and inconsistencies himself, not teaching it to an imaginary student.

How long Feynman had been dead before a video first attached his name to a technique he never described.

The notebook was real. The technique named after it was invented by somebody else, long after.

Sources:
- https://www.scotthyoung.com/blog/2011/09/01/learn-faster/ - Read in full. Confirms Scott Young posted the first video of his free 'Learning on Steroids' bootcamp, titled 'The Feynman Technique', on 1 September 2011, describing the method as picking a concept, writing an explanation simple enough to teach to a child, and returning to the source material wherever the explanation breaks down.
- https://www.scotthyoung.com/blog/2024/03/26/5-keys-feynman-technique/ - Read in full. Young's own words, written thirteen years after he coined the name: 'the technique itself is only loosely based on Richard Feynman's practices'.
- https://calnewport.com/the-feynman-notebook-method/ - Read in full. Quotes James Gleick's biography Genius directly: after his second year of graduate school at Princeton, before his oral exams, Feynman opened a notebook titled 'NOTEBOOK OF THINGS I DON'T KNOW ABOUT' and spent weeks disassembling each branch of physics to find the gaps in his own understanding.
